clue.text: Judge is playing with them about right-on comedian

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the judge and jumbled letters go around the next piece
playing with letters means toying with their order, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: right-on, meaning correct or approved, is OK

explanation.surface: A judge fooling around with some trendy, politically correct stand-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing with' turns IS THEM into ESMITH; J and ESMITH then go 'about' OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokesmith is a maker of gags, a professional humorist or stand-up performer.

clue.text: Comedians losing way may get these!

definitions.text: Comedians losing way may get these!

indicators.note: losing means the following item is dropped from the comedians' word

parts.note: jesters are court comedians
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Comics who have lost their touch can expect a hostile crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops ST from JESTERS; the whole clue is also the definition, since failing comics get booed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeers are mocking shouts, the derision an unfunny performer receives from an audience.

clue.text: Small animals almost strained equipment at the top

indicators.note: in a down entry, at the top means the equipment comes first, above the rest

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for strained is cut off

parts.note: strained means tense

explanation.surface: Little creatures nearly worn out by the gear piled on top of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TENSE to TENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittens are young cats, so they are small animals by any measure.

clue.text: That woman gets brooch repaired around Northern Dutch city

parts.note: that woman is she

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
repaired means fixed by being put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman has her brooch mended somewhere in the north of the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is fodder, not a link word. 'Northern' reads as describing the city, which is actually in the southern Netherlands; it only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of the province of North Brabant, a city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Regarding quantity of heat required to bottle nitrogen

indicators.note: to bottle is to contain, so the gas goes inside

parts.note: heat in the sense of hot temper, a measure of anger, is ire
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A physics question about how much heat it takes to bottle a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' is a link word; heat as in a heated temper gives IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is a Latin phrase used in letters and law to mean concerning or on the matter of.

clue.text: Worker unhappy about edition that's passed on

indicators.note: about means the worker and the unhappy word together surround the next piece

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A disgruntled employee grumbling over a new edition of something inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed down is bequeathed or passed from one generation to the next, an heirloom or tradition.

clue.text: Arm or leg? Nothing more needed for type of dancing

indicators.note: says the answer needs one more letter to become the dance, so that letter is taken off the dance

parts.note: limbo is the Caribbean dance under a lowered bar
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dancer asks which body part counts, then hears nothing else is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Add O to the answer and you get LIMBO, so the parse removes O from LIMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or a leg is each an example of a limb, a jointed appendage of the body.

clue.text: Copy? I will get it in China

indicators.note: in means the small word goes inside the friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, a friend

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a counterfeit can be had in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China capitalised suggests the country; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce, so it is a synonym of the verb copy.

clue.text: Mistress to play false around excited male

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps the next piece

parts.note: to belie is to misrepresent or give a false impression

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lover deceives someone about an aroused man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play false' is one verb, to belie, rather than playing as in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Belle amie is French for a beautiful friend, used for a female lover or kept woman.

clue.text: Equipment provided for building on the Strand?

definitions.text: Equipment provided for building on the Strand?

parts.words: Equipment provided for building on the Strand?
parts.note: strand means a beach, so the building is of sandcastles, done with a child's pail and shovel

explanation.surface: Sounds like construction gear for an office block on London's Strand, a famous street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a major London street, but strand also means shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail and small shovel are the classic seaside toys for making sandcastles on the shore.

clue.text: Like venture capitalist, uncomfortably plain re: return after investing with energy repeatedly

indicators.note: uncomfortably means awkwardly placed, so the letters are rearranged
repeatedly means the energy letter is taken more than once, here twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A financier is awkwardly unremarkable about returns on investment, though very energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncomfortably' covers the whole pool, the two Es included; 'after investing with' is surface padding that only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture capitalist backs risky new businesses, the hallmark of an enterprising, business-founding spirit.

clue.text: Director abandoning teams — cheers the rest

indicators.note: abandoning means the director is left out of the teams' word

parts.note: sides are teams
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A manager leaves the squads, says thanks, and the others get a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a short period of sleep or rest.

clue.text: Jewellery expert left following insolence? Exactly the reverse

indicators.note: following, with the clue's 'Exactly the reverse', puts left after insolence and the expert last

parts.note: neck is cheek or insolence
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A jewellery specialist walks out after rudeness, or perhaps it was the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exactly the reverse' swaps the clue's order: left comes after insolence and before expert, rather than expert-left following insolence.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is an ornament worn around the neck, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Excitedly rate tucking into hot broth (unusual dish)

indicators.note: tucking into means the rearranged word goes inside the rest

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in an odd way
excitedly means in an agitated way, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly rates a bowl of soup they are tucking into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excitedly' makes EART from RATE, 'unusual' makes THROB from BROTH; EART goes 'tucking into' H+THROB.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for an attractive person, which is exactly what a heart-throb is.

clue.text: Animal chatter I'd recalled was taking a different line

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the string of words runs backwards

parts.note: a deer is an animal
gas is idle talk or chatter
I'd contracted is written ID

explanation.surface: A pet's babbling remembered as it wandered off in another direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DEER GAS ID backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a different line is to hold an opposing view, to differ in opinion.

clue.text: Made inedible with teeth, though one tucks in

indicators.note: tucks in means slips inside, so the single letter goes into the word

parts.note: dentured means fitted with dentures, false teeth
a means one

explanation.surface: Food spoiled by someone's dentures, yet a diner still digs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is a link word; 'tucks in' looks like eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Denatured alcohol has been adulterated so it cannot be drunk, made unfit for consumption.

clue.text: Amount of warmth that her muff contains

indicators.note: contains means the answer sits within the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: How warm a woman's fur hand-muff keeps her.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, a hundred thousand British thermal units, used for gas billing.

clue.text: Visit — return visit?

indicators.note: a return visit read backwards from end to start is still the same quick call

parts.note: to pay a quick visit

explanation.surface: A social call, or a return call?
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads the same backwards, so a 'return' visit is still a quick drop-in.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip in is to call briefly on someone, a fleeting stop.

clue.text: Very fed up, is restricting Government in election

indicators.note: in means the restricted piece sits inside the choice

parts.note: a pick is a choice or election

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the small word encloses the letter

explanation.surface: Someone sick of the government being reined in during an election.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK opens as P+ICK to take IGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig-sick is informal British for thoroughly disgusted or fed up.

clue.text: Argument with worker about English and Scottish plant

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A dispute with an employee over English and Scottish gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree strongly associated with Scotland and its folklore.

clue.text: Adjust position of a Liberal in time in power

indicators.note: in means the pair of letters go inside

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's period in power

explanation.surface: A Liberal shifting stance while in office.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring back into line or rearrange, adjusting the alignment of something.

clue.text: Harbour workers got at bus moving the wrong way

indicators.note: moving in the wrong way suggests the letters are shuffled out of place

explanation.surface: Dockers harassed by a bus going against the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving the wrong way' looks like a reversal, but the letters are rearranged, not turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tugboats are small powerful vessels that tow and push ships in a port.

clue.text: Note stuck into a part of trellis at an angle

indicators.note: stuck into means pushed inside the next pieces

parts.note: a slat is one of the strips of a trellis

explanation.surface: A notice pinned to a wooden garden trellis, hanging crookedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means slanting or obliquely, lying askew rather than straight.

clue.text: One maintains this red wine encapsulates ultimate in taste

indicators.note: encapsulates means wraps around, so the wine holds the letter

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: ultimate in means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A wine buff insists this red holds the best of good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief that a person holds and maintains.

clue.text: Shock line included in note

indicators.note: included in means the letter goes inside

parts.note: to jot is to write a quick note

explanation.surface: A startling sentence slipped into a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolt is a sudden jarring blow or surprise, a synonym of shock.

clue.text: Further banding in body to control expanding stomach?

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
corporation is old humorous slang for a pot belly

explanation.surface: More girdling of a swelling paunch to keep it in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; banding means joining together, not belts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincorporation is forming a body or company again, banding together into one entity once more.

clue.text: Nobleman expected to throttle King

indicators.note: to throttle is to grip around the throat, so the word wraps the letter

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who was anticipated to strangle the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage, so a nobleman.

clue.text: Absolute fanatic chasing a drop of blackcurrant squash

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the absolute fanatic comes after the drop
a drop of means just a little, the first letter of the word

parts.note: utter means absolute, as in utter nonsense
a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic

explanation.surface: A total obsessive running after a splash of blackcurrant cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' in Britain is a fruit cordial, which ties to blackcurrant, but here it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut is a variety of winter squash with pale orange flesh.
